It is the amount to cut. So once you have the TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) value, which presents your bodies normal normal usage day to day doing its repairs, regular function, accounted with your activity level (sedentary as an example), you subtract the amount to cut each day.

Example: TDEE is 2300 calories and you want cut out 500 calories a day. That means you end up with 1800 calories you can consume through out the day.

Cutting 500 calories is both easy for the math and comes out to a modest weight lose rate. Here's the math and how that works, you cut those 500 calories off each day and over the period of a week that equals 3500 calories (500 * 7) that you didn't intake. That will have you at effectively ~1 lbs loss per week as 3500 calories is roughly what a pound of fat equals.

Do that and keep at it, and anyone can meet their goals in time. The point however is do this in a sustainable way akin to a life style change, if you try to cut too much and just want short term loss you wont change your life style enough and you'll likely bounce back because you did it in an unsustainable manner.
